notes.b: State income support is paid through two routes, and the route determines the conditions a claimant must meet.
points: Social insurance payments depend on a record of PRSI contributions paid while in work and are not means-tested.
Jobseeker's Benefit is the main social insurance payment for an unemployed person who has enough paid contributions.
Social assistance payments are means-tested: the household's income and savings are assessed, and no contribution record is required.
Jobseeker's Allowance is the main social assistance payment for an unemployed person who does not qualify for Jobseeker's Benefit or whose benefit has ended.
A Jobseeker's Allowance claimant must be unemployed, capable of work, available for full-time work and genuinely seeking employment.
Supplementary Welfare Allowance is a means-tested payment for people whose income does not meet their basic needs.
Child Benefit is paid for each qualifying child and is not means-tested, so it reaches families on every income level.
Payments for lone parents are means-tested and recognise that one adult is carrying the full cost of the household.
The Working Family Payment is a tax-free, means-tested payment for low-paid workers who have a dependent child.
Means-tested payments are reduced as income rises, so the household gains less from extra earnings than the wage itself.
The Fuel Allowance is paid to qualifying households to help with heating costs during the winter season.

notes.h: Schemes that reduce expenditure for low-income families
points: Medical card: gives free GP visits and access to certain health services; eligibility depends on income and health needs.
Back to School Clothing and Footwear Allowance: a once-yearly payment that helps families meet the cost of school uniforms and shoes.
Household Benefits Package: an energy allowance and related benefits for qualifying older people and people with certain disabilities or long-term illnesses.
Free pre-school place (ECCE): an early-learning place before primary school, which reduces childcare costs for families.
Housing Assistance Payment: a means-tested payment made through the local authority to help households pay rent in the private rented sector.
Money Advice and Budgeting Service (MABS): a free, confidential, State-funded service that helps people in debt, mainly low-income households, to budget and deal with creditors.

notes.b: These initiatives work through training, business supports and job creation rather than income support alone.
points: Enterprise Ireland helps Irish-owned companies increase sales, exports and employment through grants, market advice and training.
Local Enterprise Offices in each county give training, mentoring and grants to people starting or expanding small businesses.
SOLAS is the State further education and training authority; it funds, plans and coordinates further education and training through the Education and Training Boards.
SOLAS supports apprenticeships, vocational courses and literacy, numeracy and digital training, matching the skills of unemployed people to vacancies.
Work-based learning and CV and job-search preparation give unemployed people the experience that employers ask for.

notes.h: Initiatives encouraging foreign investment (Higher Level only)
notes.b: Foreign direct investment is investment by an overseas company that sets up or expands operations in Ireland.
points: IDA Ireland is the State agency that attracts overseas companies and supports them through grants, site selection and advice.
A low corporation tax rate is a key incentive for multinational companies to locate in Ireland.
A young, educated, English-speaking workforce and access to the European Union's single market attract multinational firms.
Foreign investment creates direct jobs and tax revenue and brings new skills into local labour markets, reducing unemployment.
Dependence on a few large multinationals is a weakness: if a parent company closes or moves a plant, a local area can lose many jobs at once.
Multinational employment is often concentrated in larger towns and cities, so rural areas benefit less from it.

questions.prompt: Distinguish between social insurance and social assistance payments, giving one example of each.
questions.model: Social insurance payments depend on a record of PRSI contributions paid while in work and are not means-tested. Example: Jobseeker's Benefit for a worker who has lost a job and has enough paid contributions. Social assistance payments are based on need, assessed through a means test of the household's income and savings, and do not depend on contributions. Example: Jobseeker's Allowance for an unemployed person who does not qualify for Jobseeker's Benefit.

questions.prompt: Discuss the statutory responses to poverty in Ireland. Refer to social welfare payments, at least one scheme that reduces costs for low-income families, and the role of foreign investment in creating employment.
questions.model: Social welfare: social insurance payments depend on PRSI contributions, while social assistance payments such as Jobseeker's Allowance and Supplementary Welfare Allowance are means-tested and paid on the basis of need; Child Benefit is universal for each qualifying child; the Working Family Payment supports low-paid working families with a dependent child. Schemes reducing costs: the medical card gives free GP visits to those who meet income and health criteria; the Back to School Clothing and Footwear Allowance helps with uniforms and shoes; the Fuel Allowance helps with heating costs; the Housing Assistance Payment helps with rent in the private rented sector; the free pre-school place (ECCE) reduces childcare costs. Each scheme addresses a specific cost pressure that would otherwise push a family into poverty. Foreign investment: foreign direct investment is investment by overseas companies in Irish operations; IDA Ireland attracts it with grants, site selection and advice; a low corporation tax rate and a skilled, English-speaking workforce are key attractions; it creates direct jobs, tax revenue and new skills, reducing unemployment. Limitations: dependence on a few large multinationals exposes local areas to sudden job losses when plants close; multinational jobs are concentrated in larger towns and cities, so rural areas gain less. Assessment: income supports relieve immediate hardship, while investment and employment supports address the root cause of unemployment, so the two work best together.
